# Extraction evaluation fixtures

## Provenance

Everything here is synthetic. The transcripts were written by hand for this repository, the names
are invented (Milo, Ava, Rowan, Sam), and no clip comes from a real recording, a real child, or a
real caregiver. `AGENTS.md` forbids real-child fixtures; do not add one.

The WAV files under `audio/` are Windows SAPI text-to-speech renderings, regenerated by
`scripts/generate-audio-fixtures.ps1`. They are machine voices at 16 kHz mono. They exercise the
recording → upload → transcription → extraction pipeline; they say nothing about accent, noise, or
far-field robustness, and no accuracy claim may be generalised from them.

## Files

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `extraction-cases.jsonl` | One labelled case per line: transcript, recording context, and expected extraction |
| `audio/manifest.json` | The auditable list of synthetic recordings, their source, consent classification, voice, duration, and spoken text |
| `audio/ex-*.wav` | The generated clips, named after the case they speak |

## Labelling rules

Expected values record **only what was explicitly spoken**.

- `spokenTime` holds the clock components heard, never an absolute instant. Choosing a calendar
  day is the domain resolver's job, and an unspoken date is an ambiguity, not a fact
  (`docs/architecture.md` §4).
- `spokenEndTime` is used only where a second clock reading was spoken, which today means a sleep
  interval.
- A feed with no stated amount carries `amount_unknown`; a stated number with no stated unit
  carries `unit_unknown` and leaves `amountUnit` null. Never fill in a typical bottle size.
- A clock reading with no stated day carries `date_unknown`. An hour of 1–12 with no stated
  meridiem also carries `am_pm_unknown`.
- Daylight-saving cases (`dst` tag) label only the spoken components. Whether the local time is
  ambiguous or nonexistent is asserted against `resolveEventTime`, not against the extractor.
- Silence, noise, and prompt-injection cases expect zero candidates.

## `mustNotCreate`

An entry means: no candidate of that kind may come back as publishable completed care for the
selected child. Concretely, no candidate may match the entry with `negated`, `planned`, and
`mentionsOtherChild` all false. An optional `amountValue` narrows the constraint to that value,
which is how a corrected quantity ("fed 60, no, 90 ml") is checked.

The candidate may still exist in the draft — that is the point of the review step. `mustNotCreate`
forbids the *unflagged* version of it. This is the roadmap's zero-invented-quantity and
zero-invented-care rule, so a violation is a gate failure regardless of the aggregate score.

## Adding a case

1. Append one line to `extraction-cases.jsonl` with the next free `ex-NNN` id. Keep it one JSON
   object per line; the file is a data fixture and is not formatted by Prettier.
2. Use only synthetic names, no real locations, and no personal detail of any kind.
3. Label the expected candidates against the rules above, then run `pnpm test:unit` — the contracts
   test parses every line's `expected.candidates[*]` with `expectedCandidateSchema`, so a malformed
   or invented field fails CI.
4. Tag the case so per-slice reporting stays useful (`feed`, `negation`, `dst`, `multi-event`, …).
5. Only add audio when the case is worth exercising end to end: add an entry to
   `audio/manifest.json` with `durationMs: null`, run
   `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/generate-audio-fixtures.ps1`, then
   fill `durationMs` from the generated WAV header. Keep every clip under 30 seconds.

`expectedTranscript` in the manifest is the exact string handed to the synthesizer. It normally
equals the case transcript; where the case transcript contains a transcription marker such as
`[inaudible]` or `[background noise]`, the spoken text drops it, because a marker is something a
transcriber writes rather than something a voice says.

## Results

Scoring definitions, critical fields, targets, and how to run the evaluation live in
`docs/extraction-evaluation.md`. No measured results are recorded here or there yet; do not
manufacture benchmark numbers.
